name: Power Sequence
description: Let's call a list of positive integers $$$a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1}$$$ a power sequence if there is a positive integer $$$c$$$, so that for every $$$0 \le i \le n-1$$$ then $$$a_i = c^i$$$. Given a list of $$$n$$$ positive integers $$$a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1}$$$, you are allowed to: Reorder the list (i.e. pick a permutation $$$p$$$ of $$$\{0,1,...,n - 1\}$$$ and change $$$a_i$$$ to $$$a_{p_i}$$$), then Do the following operation any number of times: pick an index $$$i$$$ and change $$$a_i$$$ to $$$a_i - 1$$$ or $$$a_i + 1$$$ (i.e. increment or decrement $$$a_i$$$ by $$$1$$$) with a cost of $$$1$$$. Find the minimum cost to transform $$$a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1}$$$ into a power sequence.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: Print the minimum cost to transform $$$a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1}$$$ into a power sequence.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.
